A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-doc.md:109:Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts
`--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCP
JAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage err
or (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and doe
s not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order pick
s another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it
still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, a
nd exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-doc.md:
123:Empty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK
eval reporting only).\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:335:Run the Cross-App Access (ID-JAG) debugger: self-issue an ID-J
AG, redeem it at the target authorization server (RFC 7523), and call the MCP server with the resulting access token. See the [XAA
Debugger guide](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/xaa.md) for the trust setup, registration strategies, and CI usage.\n/workspace/mcpja
m-eval/cli-reference.md:569:An unknown ID, or an ID or flag for a suite the run leaves out, is a usage error (exit code `2`) befor
e anything runs.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:597:| `--server <name=url>` | | Bind a target server to an HTTP(S) URL.
Repeatable. Split on the first `=`; duplicate or unknown names are usage errors. |\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:611:Gl
obal `--timeout` bounds each setup operation and MCP request, not the whole run. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed, `2` usage/uns
upported/import/policy, `3` credentials, `4` setup/billing/artifact, `5` inconclusive or interrupted — see [Exit codes](https://do
cs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md#exit-codes).\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:643:`--host` is a usage error rather than a
silent precedence rule.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:1186:Launch a goal run. **Spends model credits** — fans out into
`targets × iterations` chat sessions.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:1193:| `--expected-sponsored <n>` | No | How many
of this launch's conversations you expect to be sponsored (paid from MCPJam's per-user allowance instead of your organization's cr
edits). If the actual split differs, the launch is refused with a `409` and nothing is created. Omit to accept whatever split appl
ies. |\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:1441:Grade a saved server against a publisher's directory as the platform reaches
it — through the saved server row and the authorize exchange. This is the hosted half of `readiness check`: it answers a different

ith MCPJam — no credits are consumed), and leaves a persistent record.\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:1461:| `--ai-obser
vations` | No | Add optional model observations. **Consumes MCPJam credits.** |\n/workspace/mcpjam-eval/cli-reference.md:1477:| `-
